courses.title: Advanced Chemical Communication
courses.description: Fundamental and advanced techniques used for accessing, interpreting, and communicating chemical information. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced Instrumental Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Applications of advanced instrumental analysis to explore problems associated with analytical, organic, inorganic, physical and biochemistry.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced Chemical Equilibria and Kinetics
courses.description: Advanced chemical equilibria including acid-base concepts, pH, and application to physical and physical organic chemistry.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at graduate level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced treatment of quantum mechanics and quantum field theory of chemical problems including variation, perturbation, and computational methods.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Chemical Spectroscopy and Characterization
courses.description: Application of electronic, vibrational (IR/Raman), rotational, and nuclear spectroscopies, scattering methods and atomic force microscopy to characterization of matter
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Chemical Kinetics
courses.description: Kinetics and mechanisms of chemical reactions including transition state theory, collision theory, photochemical excitation and dissociation, solvation effects, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Synthetic Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Study of main group and transition group organic reactions with focus on reagents, mechanisms, stereochemistry and retro-synthetic analysis as applied to multi-step synthesis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Theoretical and practical study of experimental techniques used by organic chemists to investigate problems in reaction mechanisms, catalysis, solution chemistry and substituent effects.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Current Advances in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Recent advances in topics in a select area of organic chemistry are examined: for example, reaction mechanisms, spectroscopy, heterocycles, natural products, organometallic, bioorganic, industrial and photochemistry. May be taken up to five times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 15 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Biochemistry
courses.description: Examination of advanced and selected topics in biochemistry with topics ranging from protein conjugation, post-translation modification of proteins, nucleic acid metabolism, the omics (e.g. , proteomics, genomics, glycomics, and lipidomics), bioinorganic chemistry, bioorganic chemistry, advanced membrane dynamics, photosynthesis, anaerobic metabolic pathways, biosynthesis, signaling, and neurotransmitter biochemistry. May be taken up to five times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 15 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced modern concepts of inorganic chemistry, which will build on concepts introduced in CHM 4010, including bonding, reactivity and spectroscopy in physical inorganic and organometallic chemistry, with a focus on applying theory to current research.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Current Advances in Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Modern concepts of inorganic chemistry, which may include organometallic chemistry, bioinorganic chemistry, computational chemistry, spectroscopy, solid-state chemistry, or f-element chemistry, with a focus on current chemical literature. May be taken up to five times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 15 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Instrumental Analysis
courses.description: Theory and application of instrumental analysis in contemporary areas such as pharmaceutical chemistry, environmental chemistry, food chemistry and clinical chemistry from the perspective of an analytical chemist.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Water Sampling and Analysis
courses.description: Chemical principles that govern the reactions, transport, effects, and fates of chemical species in water, including sampling techniques and analytical methods.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students Activity
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students Laboratory
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Modern concepts of inorganic chemistry, including group theory; solid-state chemistry; orbitals; bonding theory; molecular structure; electronic structure and spectra; main group and transition metal chemistry; acid/base and redox chemistry; coordination chemistry; thermodynamics; kinetics and mechanisms; organometallics; and catalysis. Required for certification by the American Chemical Society.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 ; or CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 ; or CHM 313 or CHM 305.

courses.title: Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Types of polymers and polymerization reactions; properties of polymer solutions and the determination of molecular weights; elasticity and other bulk properties.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Reaction Kinetics
courses.description: Kinetics and mechanisms of chemical reactions including transition state theory, collision theory, photochemical excitation and dissociation, solvation effects, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 , or CHM 3050 .

courses.title: Introduction to Colloid and Surface Chemistry
courses.description: Examination of gas-liquid, gas-solid, solid-liquid interfaces, as well as adsorption and surface area determination, the electrical double layer and its relation to colloidal stability, and electro-kinetic phenomena.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 305, CHM 313, CHM 3040 or CHM 3110 .

courses.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
courses.description: Advanced treatment of chemical thermodynamics, and the relationship between chemical potential, molecular structure, and statistical mechanics
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 , or CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 , or CHM 313 or CHM 305.

courses.title: Macromolecular Modeling
courses.description: Theoretical studies and applications of computational techniques to macromolecular (e.g., polymers, proteins, and nucleic acids) structure, stability and function.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 2600 ; and CHM 327, CHM 3270W , CHM 321 or CHM 3210 .

courses.title: Computational Biochemistry
courses.description: Computational methods in modern biochemistry including sequence entry and editing, sequence alignment, phylogenetic analysis, homology searching, elementary protein structure prediction, and evaluation of 3-D molecular structures
courses.prerequisites: CHM 2600 ; and CHM 327, CHM 3270W , CHM 321, CHM 3210 or BIO 4300 .

courses.title: Methods for Data Acquisition and Analysis
courses.description: Theoretical concepts required for the collection and analysis of data, along with experimental considerations for implementation of particle/electron/photon counting for quantitative analysis are explored.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 , CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 , CHM 313 or CHM 305 and CHM 352L or CHM 3520L .

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced treatment of quantum chemistry emphasizing approximation methods
courses.prerequisites: CHM 3050 , CHM 3120 , CHM 305 or CHM 313.

courses.title: Computational Chemistry
courses.description: Applied quantum mechanical studies of molecular geometries; electronic excited states, potential energy surfaces, and conformational structures are explored

courses.title: Solution Equilibria in Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Study of advanced acid-base theory, complexation, nonaqueous acid-base, solvent extraction and ion-exchange equilibria
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Organic Synthesis
courses.description: An advanced theoretical and practical study of modern methodologies and strategies in synthetic organic chemistry.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 , C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L , D or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 , and D or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Organic Synthesis Laboratory
courses.description: An advanced laboratory course focusing on multistep organic syntheses. Utilization of modern techniques to synthesize, purify and characterize organic compounds. Corequisite(s): CHM 4220 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 , C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L , D or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 , and D or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Theoretical and practical study of experimental techniques used by organic chemists to investigate problems in reaction mechanisms, catalysis, solution chemistry and substituent effects.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Theoretical and practical study of experimental techniques used by organic chemists to investigate problems in reaction mechanisms, catalysis, solution chemistry and substituent effects. Corequisite(s): CHM 4230 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Organic Analysis
courses.description: Advanced treatment of modern methods for the structural determination of organic compounds. Emphasis will be on spectroscopic methods, but classical functional group analysis will also be explored. Spectroscopic methods include IR, 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, advanced NMR experiments (e.g., DEPT, HETCOR, COSY, HMBC, NOESY), and mass spectrometry.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Organic Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Purification and structure determination of organic compounds using modern techniques and spectroscopic methods as well as classical functional group analysis. Projects include natural product isolation and separation and identification of mixtures of unknowns. Corequisite(s): CHM 4240 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Internship in Chemistry
courses.description: On-the-job training and work experience in the chemistry field under the guidance of a faculty internship coordinator and on-site job supervisor. The internship is arranged by the student and may not be a continuation of an ongoing job or volunteer experience. A minimum of 4 hours per week (60 hours/semester) per unit credit. Grade will be based on a written evaluation from the job supervisor and an evaluation of the student presentation and/or written report by the internship coordinator. Student must be enrolled in CHM 4410 during the term in which work at the internship site is done. Hours worked in one term may not carry over into another. A maximum of 4 units of CHM 4410 may be allowed as elective units for each option in chemistry (ACS approved, biochemistry or general). May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of 60 units, Overall GPA 2.0 or higher and Signed application.

courses.title: Modern Mass Spectrometry and FT-NMR
courses.description: Introduction of the theoretical and practical applications of one- and two-dimensional NMR and mass spectrometry, including instrumentation and spectral interpretation. Gain basic understanding of a variety of NMR pulse sequences and have a fundamental and technical understanding of ionization sources, mass analyzers, and their limitations.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 342 or CHM 3420 ; C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Environmental Analysis
courses.description: Sample collection and preparation techniques for different environmental media, such as water, air, and soil. Instrumental analysis of various environmental samples. Corequisite(s): CHM 4490L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 2210 and CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Environmental Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Instrumental analysis of various environmental samples collected from different environmental media, such as water, air, and soil. Corequisite(s): CHM 4490 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 2210 and CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Bioanalytical Chemistry
courses.description: Analytical techniques used in the study of problems in biotechnology and clinical medicine. Uniqueness of problems inherent to the analysis of biological samples, contemporary methodologies and techniques.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 327 or CHM 3270W ; C- or better in CHM 327L or CHM 3270LW ; C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; and C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L .

courses.title: Enzymology
courses.description: Detailed examination of the structure, function, kinetics, inhibition, and regulation of enzymes. Corequisite(s): CHM 4510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 ; and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3280L .

courses.title: Enzymology Laboratory
courses.description: Experimental aspects of advanced enzyme kinetics and inhibition. Corequisite(s): CHM 4510 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 ; and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3280L .

courses.title: Advanced Biomolecular Structure
courses.description: Examines the relationships between the structure and function of the major biomolecules.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 ; and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3280L .

courses.title: Informational Biomolecules and Recombinant DNA
courses.description: Mechanisms of information transfer in biochemistry including the molecular details of DNA replication, DNA recombination, DNA repair, RNA transcription, protein synthesis, and recombinant techniques.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 .

courses.title: Advanced Metabolism
courses.description: Detailed examination of advanced metabolic pathways, mechanisms, and regulation.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3280 .

courses.title: Green Chemistry
courses.description: Principles and important concepts of green chemistry. Exploration of how organic chemistry, product development, plant safety, market development, environmental impacts, and financial incentives holistically affect the development of green processes and cleaner technologies.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 316 or CHM 3150 ; and C- or better in CHM 319L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Air Pollution Problems
courses.description: Concepts of air pollution: major air pollutants; sources; future problems.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 221 or CHM 2210 ; C- or better in CHM 221L or CHM 2210L ; and CHM 305, CHM 313, CHM 3040 and CHM 3050 , or CHM 3110 and CHM 3120 .

courses.description: Research in area of specialization conducted as part of the preparation for writing a thesis under the direction of a faculty member. Total credit limited to 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units.

courses.description: Compilation, evaluation, interpretation and report of research for thesis. Completion of approved, bound thesis. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or instructor consent.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
